claims.evidence: OpenStax 7.2: adult skull has 22 bones; brain case and facial bones are the two groups. StatPearls: 22 bones in two regions.
OpenStax 7.2: brain case surrounds and protects the brain; facial bones give the face its structure and form the jaws. 'Houses' dropped.
claims.newSentence: The brain case surrounds and protects the brain, while the facial bones give the face its structure and form the upper and lower jaws.

claims.evidence: OpenStax 7.2: 21 bones immobile and united into one unit, mandible the only movable bone. OpenStax 9.2: skull sutures are fibrous joints.
claims.newSentence: Only the mandible, or lower jaw, is movable; the other bones are immobile and united into a single unit by fibrous joints called sutures.

claims.evidence: Site-side: atlas.json has the 22 skull bones as separate structures plus Hyoid bone. OpenStax 7.2: hyoid does not contact other bones, not part of skull.
OpenStax 7.2 and chapter review: 22 bones; brain case has eight bones; facial bones number 14.
OpenStax chapter review: brain case is paired parietal and temporal plus unpaired frontal, occipital, sphenoid and ethmoid bones.
OpenStax chapter review: paired maxillary, palatine, zygomatic, nasal, lacrimal, inferior conchae; unpaired vomer and mandible.
OpenStax 7.2: mandible is the only moveable skull bone. OpenStax 9.6: mandibular condyle articulates with the temporal bone at the TMJ.
OpenStax 7.2: coronal, sagittal, lambdoid and squamous sutures each described.
OpenStax key terms and chapter review: anterior, middle and posterior cranial fossae; foramen magnum in the posterior fossa.
NHS inform: CT image shows bleeding, bruising or swelling in the brain; skull x-rays are not carried out anymore. 'Plain' dropped.
claims.newSentence: CT scan for a severe head injury; skull X-rays are not carried out any more

claims.evidence: StatPearls skull: neurocranium protects the brain, viscerocranium forms the face. 'Houses' changed to 'protects'; brain case synonym per OpenStax.
claims.newSentence: The skull has two regions: the neurocranium, or brain case, which protects the brain, and the viscerocranium, which forms the face.

claims.evidence: OpenStax chapter review: brain case is eight bones, paired parietal and temporal plus unpaired frontal, occipital, sphenoid, ethmoid.
OpenStax chapter review: 14 facial bones; paired maxillary, palatine, zygomatic, nasal, lacrimal, inferior conchae; unpaired vomer and mandible.
OpenStax chapter review: ethmoid is a brain case bone and also contributes to the formation of facial structures.
claims.newSentence: The ethmoid is counted among the cranial bones but also contributes to the formation of facial structures.

claims.evidence: OpenStax 7.2: hyoid is an independent bone that does not contact any other bone and thus is not part of the skull.
claims.newSentence: The hyoid bone is an independent bone that does not contact any other bone and so is not part of the skull.

claims.evidence: OpenStax 9.2: skull sutures are narrow fibrous joints; connective tissue holds adjacent skull bones together.
OpenStax 7.2: coronal suture runs side to side across the skull and joins the parietal bones to the frontal bone.
OpenStax 7.2: sagittal suture extends back from the coronal suture along the top midline, joining the parietal bones. 'Ends at lambdoid' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: The sagittal suture extends backwards from the coronal suture, running along the midline at the top of the skull, and joins the two parietal bones.

claims.evidence: OpenStax 7.2: lambdoid suture joins the occipital bone to the right and left parietal and temporal bones; draft omitted temporal.
claims.newSentence: The lambdoid suture joins the occipital bone to the right and left parietal and temporal bones.

claims.evidence: OpenStax 7.2: squamous suture unites the squamous portion of the temporal bone with the parietal bone.
claims.newSentence: The squamous suture unites the squamous part of the temporal bone with the parietal bone.

claims.evidence: OpenStax 9.2 and review: skull sutures are functionally synarthroses, some allow slight movement; synarthrosis is an essentially immobile joint. Draft said 'a few'.
claims.newSentence: Skull sutures are functionally classed as synarthroses, which are essentially immobile joints, although some allow slight movement.

claims.evidence: OpenStax 7.2: the 22nd bone is the mandible, which is the only moveable bone of the skull.
OpenStax 7.2: mandible has a horizontal body and vertical ramus on each side; the outside margin where they meet is the angle.
claims.newSentence: The mandible has a horizontal body and a vertical ramus on each side, and the outer margin where they join is the angle.

claims.evidence: OpenStax 7.2: coronoid process gives attachment to a biting muscle; condylar process is topped by the oval condyle. 'Flattened' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: The coronoid process on the ramus gives attachment to one of the biting muscles, while the condylar process is topped by the oval condyle.

claims.evidence: OpenStax 9.6: mandibular condyle articulates with the mandibular fossa and articular tubercle of the temporal bone; articular disc lies between.
OpenStax 9.6 and key terms: TMJ allows depression/elevation (opening/closing the mouth), protraction/retraction and side-to-side motions of the mandible.
claims.newSentence: The joint allows the mandible to be lowered and raised, which opens and closes the mouth, to move forwards and backwards, and to move from side to side.

claims.evidence: OpenStax 11.3: masseter is the main chewing muscle, elevates the mandible to close the mouth; origin zygomatic arch. Arch-formation clause dropped.
claims.newSentence: The masseter, the main muscle used for chewing, arises from the zygomatic arch and raises the mandible to close the mouth.

claims.evidence: OpenStax key terms and review: anterior fossa shallowest, posterior deepest, middle between; three fossae form the cranial floor.
OpenStax key terms: anterior cranial fossa is the shallowest, extending from the frontal bone to the lesser wing of the sphenoid.
claims.newSentence: The anterior fossa is the shallowest and extends from the frontal bone to the lesser wings of the sphenoid.

claims.evidence: OpenStax chapter review: middle fossa floor holds optic canal, superior orbital fissure, foramina rotundum, ovale and spinosum; runs back from lesser wings.
OpenStax chapter review: posterior fossa is deepest, extends to occipital bone; openings include foramen magnum, internal acoustic meatus, jugular foramina, hypoglossal canals.
StatPearls: skull base has many holes and fissures for neural and vascular passage; cranial nerves and some vessels exit via foramina.
claims.newSentence: The skull base has many openings through which nerves and blood vessels pass.

claims.evidence: StatPearls: foramen magnum is the largest cranial foramen; contents include brainstem and vertebral arteries. 'Brain connects with cord' not stated.
claims.newSentence: The foramen magnum is the largest of the cranial foramina, and its contents include the brainstem and the vertebral arteries.

claims.evidence: StatPearls optic canal page: the canal carries the optic nerve, the ophthalmic artery and sympathetic fibres.
OpenStax: orbit walls built from seven bones (frontal, zygomatic, maxillary, palatine, ethmoid, lacrimal, sphenoid); orbit is the eye socket housing eyeball and its muscles.
claims.newSentence: Seven bones contribute to the walls of each orbit, or eye socket, which houses the eyeball and the muscles that move it: the frontal, zygomatic, maxillary, palatine, ethmoid, lacrimal and sphenoid bones.

claims.evidence: OpenStax: septum divides nasal cavity; formed by ethmoid perpendicular plate (upper portion), vomer and septal cartilage. Lower and front positions not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: The nasal septum divides the nasal cavity into halves and is formed by the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid bone, which makes up its upper portion, together with the vomer and septal cartilage.

claims.evidence: OpenStax: sinuses in frontal, maxillary, sphenoid, ethmoid bones; frontal most anterior, maxillary largest below orbits, sphenoid most posterior. 'Above eyebrows' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: The paranasal sinuses sit within the frontal, maxillary, sphenoid and ethmoid bones: the frontal sinus is the most anterior, the maxillary sinuses, below the orbits, are the largest, and the sphenoid sinus is the most posterior.

claims.evidence: OpenStax key terms: ethmoid air cells are small air-filled spaces in the ethmoid, between the orbit and upper nasal cavity.
OpenStax 7.5: fontanelles are large areas of dense connective tissue between brain case bones. 'Not yet fused' and 'soft spots' not stated.
claims.newSentence: At birth, large areas of dense connective tissue called fontanelles lie between the bones of the brain case.

claims.evidence: OpenStax 7.5: fontanelles give the skull flexibility during birth, letting it change shape in the birth canal. Bones 'overlap' elaboration not confirmed.
claims.newSentence: The fontanelles provide flexibility to the skull during birth, allowing it to change shape as it passes through the birth canal.

claims.evidence: OpenStax 7.5: fontanelles allow continued skull growth after birth, decrease in size and disappear (source gives an age). 'As brain enlarges' not quoted.
claims.newSentence: After birth the fontanelles allow for continued growth of the skull, and they decrease in size and eventually disappear.

claims.evidence: OpenStax 7.5: flat bones of brain case form by intramembranous ossification; brain case floor by endochondral ossification (cartilage model converted to bone).
claims.newSentence: The flat bones of the brain case form by intramembranous ossification, in which mesenchyme cells differentiate directly into bone-producing cells, whereas the floor of the brain case forms by endochondral ossification, in which a cartilage model is gradually converted into bone.

claims.evidence: OpenStax 9.2: bony fusion of sutures is called synostosis; sagittal, coronal and lambdoid sutures begin to ossify and fuse in later life.
claims.newSentence: Late in life the sagittal, coronal and lambdoid sutures begin to ossify and fuse, a change called synostosis, or bony fusion.

claims.evidence: NHS inform: most skull fractures heal by themselves, particularly simple linear fractures; healing can take many months.
StatPearls: pterion joins frontal, parietal, temporal, sphenoid above the ear; blunt trauma can lacerate the middle meningeal artery (maxillary branch), causing epidural haematoma.
StatPearls skull page, retrieved twice: arterial haemorrhage in the epidural space accumulates quickly and does not cross suture lines.
OpenStax 9.6: causes listed are arthritis, wearing of articular cartilage, muscle fatigue from overuse or teeth grinding, articular disc damage, jaw injury. 'Painful' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: Temporomandibular joint disorder can arise from arthritis, wearing of the articular cartilage, muscle fatigue from overuse or grinding of the teeth, damage to the articular disc or a jaw injury.

claims.evidence: NHS: symptoms include pain around the jaw, ear and temple, and clicking, popping or grinding sounds when moving the jaw.
claims.newSentence: The NHS lists pain around the jaw, ear and temple, and clicking, popping or grinding sounds when the jaw moves, among the symptoms of temporomandibular disorder.

claims.evidence: NHS: most head injuries not serious; get help for any symptoms. 999 list: head wound with something inside, dent, clear fluid from ears or nose.
claims.newSentence: Most head injuries are not serious, but the NHS says it is important to get medical help for any symptoms. The NHS lists a head wound with something inside it, a dent to the head and clear fluid coming from the ears or nose among the signs for which it advises calling 999.

claims.evidence: NHS inform: CT image of the head shows any bleeding, bruising or swelling in the brain. 'Used to judge seriousness' and 'in hospital' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: For a severe head injury, a CT scan produces a detailed image of the inside of the head that shows whether there is any bleeding, bruising or swelling in the brain.

claims.evidence: NHS inform: skull x-rays are not carried out anymore as they do not provide information on brain damage.
claims.newSentence: Skull X-rays are not carried out any more because they do not provide information on brain damage.

notes: Rule used: a sentence counts as unsupported (and was edited, not removed) when a distinct fact in it could not be confirmed and was cut (c19, c34, c37, c38, c41, c42, c51); wording-only or minor-descriptor changes count as supported with action edited. No sentence needed removal outright; no textbook, wrong or unsafe verdicts. Site-side: c04 (3D model) checked against data/hd/atlas.json (22 skull-bone structures plus Hyoid bone) and OpenStax 7.2 for the hyoid. Attribution caveat: many OpenStax facts (c05-c07, c10, c13-c15, c29-c32, c36-c39) came from the 7.2 snippet plus the Chapter 7 Review and Key Terms pages, same publisher, because the search tool truncated the 7.2 body; StatPearls facts for c33, c34, c46 and c47 came partly from sibling StatPearls pages (Skull Imaging, Skull Foramen, Middle Meningeal Arteries); the tool does not say which page held which sentence, so a human may want to open NBK499834 and NBK526041. Structure changes: the fracture-healing sentence (c45) was moved into the head-injury section, retitled 'Head injuries and skull fractures', so the NHS warning signs come first; c50 was recast as reported NHS advice in two sentences (house style 'official information advises', adds the NHS line to get medical help for any symptoms). Added references: OpenStax 11.3 (masseter) and StatPearls Middle Meningeal Arteries; optic canal URL canonicalised (report=reader removed). Believed true but not confirmed, so cut: sagittal suture ends at the lambdoid suture; frontal sinus above the eyebrows; sphenoid sinus within the sphenoid body; septal cartilage at the front and vomer below; foramen magnum as the brain to spinal cord passage; zygomatic arch formed by zygomatic and temporal bones (seen only in a PMC case report); skull bones overlapping at birth; fontanelle closure timing (source says by age 2, kept number-free; the draft's early childhood was dropped). For clinical review: c47 is stated absolutely in StatPearls (epidural bleeds can occasionally cross sutures; consider 'usually'); the OpenStax 7.5 summary also put facial bones under endochondral ossification, which disagrees with usual embryology, so only the brain case flat bones and floor are stated; OpenStax 9.2 calls sutures immobile yet notes some allow slight movement (c03 and c22 harmonised). c20 follows OpenStax, which says the lambdoid suture joins the occipital bone to the parietal and temporal bones; many anatomy texts name only the parietals (the occipitomastoid suture continues it), so a clinical reviewer may prefer the narrower wording. All 52 claims were checked (unchecked = 0); 22 of 30 searches used.
